applicable_when: The kernel is a GEMM (M=501760, N=64, K=480) fused with bias add. The B matrix has stride_bn=480 (non-power-of-2, not a multiple of 32), so when Triton stages the (BLOCK_N=64, BLOCK_K=32) B tile through shared memory, the 480-element row stride creates systematic bank aliasing — 8-way conflicts on 69.79% of all shared load wavefronts. Prior attempts to fix this by changing BLOCK_K, BLOCK_M, or num_stages all introduced correctness bugs in the executor's rewrites. The diversity instruction mandates TMA loads. On Hopper (H100), replacing tl.make_block_ptr + tl.load with tl.make_tensor_descriptor + descriptor.load() uses the TMA hardware unit, which performs asynchronous bulk copies from global memory directly into shared memory via a dedicated DMA path — bypassing the warp-level load pipeline entirely. This eliminates the bank-conflict-prone scalar staging path and offloads address generation to the TMA unit, freeing SM cycles. The existing code already uses tl.make_block_ptr (a prerequisite pattern), making the migration to tl.make_tensor_descriptor straightforward.
